hooks_key_means: Kimi reads plugin hooks from the manifest's `hooks` array, not a file: chock builds them at `hooks` (the layout every bundle merge reads) and folds that document into the manifest when the package is written.
hook_timeout_means: Kimi is not a `chock sync` vendor (no row in src/chock/data/hook_timeouts.json) and agentseam's rendering writes no timeout, so the documented `timeout` (seconds, 1-600, default 30) gets chock's 45 s here: a 30 s default would end the hook before the engine's own 30 s budget and fail open.

says: `<plugin_root>/kimi.plugin.json` / `<plugin_root>/.kimi-plugin/plugin.json`. When both files exist, `kimi.plugin.json` takes precedence.
`name` | Required; serves as the plugin id. Must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}`
`skills` | One or more `./` paths within the plugin root; if omitted, root `SKILL.md` is the single Skill root
Each entry uses the same fields as a `[[hooks]]` rule in `config.toml` (`event`, `matcher`, `command`, `timeout`)
The hook process receives two extra environment variables: `KIMI_CODE_HOME` and `KIMI_PLUGIN_ROOT` (the plugin root directory).
Each hook runs with its working directory set to the plugin root
`/plugins install <path-or-url>` | Install from a local directory, zip URL, or GitHub repository URL

Local installations are copied to `$KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/managed/<id>/`, and the CLI always runs from this managed copy. Editing the original source directory after installation has no effect; you must reinstall.
Plugins are currently installed per-user and apply to all projects; project-level installation scope is not yet supported.
Plugin changes apply after `/reload` or in new sessions.
`0` means allow, `2` means block, other non-zero values default to allow
Even if the script errors or times out, the CLI **will not interrupt your work** as a result.
should not be used as the sole security barrier
`timeout` | `integer` | No | Timeout in seconds, range 1–600; defaults to 30 seconds

silent_on: A non-interactive install: the docs name only the `/plugins` slash commands in the TUI. The shell Kimi runs hook commands with on Windows is unmeasured.
